evals.name: stop-and-run-fresh-context-adversarial-pass
evals.prompt: scrutinize don't coast — wait, stop. You just wrote the whole cache-invalidation function and moved straight on. Are you sure that's actually right?
evals.expected_output: The skill re-anchors adversarial self-scrutiny, halts the current trajectory (delta 1: stop first), and delegates the adversarial re-examination of the just-produced function to a fresh-context non-fork subagent blind to the reasoning that produced it, then surfaces the findings and remediates WITH the user (delta 2) rather than silently re-reading the code in the same context or barrelling into an autonomous rewrite.
expectations: Stops the in-flight trajectory before auditing rather than pushing the work one step further
Delegates the adversarial pass to a fresh-context (non-fork) subagent blind to the producing reasoning, not a same-context self-read
Remediates collaboratively with the user rather than launching an autonomous rewrite

evals.name: clean-pass-reported-not-fabricated
evals.prompt: scrutinize don't coast — second-guess the migration script you just produced. (It was already checked against the schema and the rollback path, and both were confirmed.)
evals.expected_output: The fresh-context adversarial pass finds the work sound, so the skill reports clean. It does not manufacture a flaw to look diligent, and it does not downgrade a genuine non-finding into a vague caveat.
expectations: Reports clean when the adversarial pass finds the work sound
Does NOT invent a fault to appear diligent
States the clean outcome plainly instead of hedging with a vague caveat

evals.name: routes-pre-implementation-plan-to-devils-advocate
evals.prompt: scrutinize don't coast — before we build any of this, poke holes in the whole migration plan I just laid out.
evals.expected_output: The skill recognizes this as stress-testing a plan BEFORE implementation, which is /planning:devils-advocate's axis, not adversarial re-examination of output already produced. It routes to devils-advocate (degrading to prose if that skill is absent) rather than treating the not-yet-built plan as produced output.
expectations: Distinguishes 'stress-test a plan before building' from re-examining already-produced output
Routes to /planning:devils-advocate (or degrades to prose guidance when it is not installed)
Does not misclassify a pre-implementation plan as finished output to scrutinize

evals.name: focus-scopes-but-does-not-suppress-outside-flaw
evals.prompt: scrutinize don't coast the security assumptions — re-examine what you just wrote, focused on the auth checks.
evals.expected_output: The skill aims the adversarial pass at the named focus (the auth/security assumptions) and treats the focus as narrowing aim, not a hard filter — it states that a serious flaw found outside the focus would still be surfaced rather than scoped out. The scoped pass runs in a fresh-context subagent.
expectations: Scopes the adversarial re-examination to the named focus (the security/auth assumptions)
Treats the focus as narrowing aim, not a hard filter — states that a serious out-of-focus flaw would still be surfaced rather than suppressed
Delegates the scoped pass to a fresh-context subagent, not a same-context re-read

evals.name: posture-set-at-conversation-start-no-fabricated-findings
evals.expected_output: Fired with no prior work to examine, the skill does only the re-anchor step: it acknowledges adversarial self-scrutiny as active for the session and stops. It manufactures no findings and runs no adversarial pass, because there is no produced output yet — matching the shared method doc's conversation-start case and the temporal-neutrality of the discipline.
expectations: Treats a no-work-yet invocation as posture-setting, not an audit
Does not manufacture findings or spawn an adversarial pass when there is nothing produced to examine
Acknowledges the discipline as active for the rest of the session
